text.p: -- Dain Bosworth Inc said Monday it initiated coverage on Photoelectron Corp with a buy recommendation for speculative, long-term investors.

-- Photoelectron, which provides a therapeutic X-ray system used to treat cancerous tumors, has an initial $800 million market opportunity for its key Photon Radiosurgery System (PRS), Dain Bosworth said. The company has filed an application for the PRS with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, and Dain Bosworth said the system could be approved for sale by third quarter 1997.

-- Photoelectron has eight U.S. patents for the PRS and other equipment, has another three pending and has been allowed two others which have yet to be issued, Dain Bosworth said. It said it is therefore comfortable with the company's ability to retain its edge over competitors.
-- Dain Bosworth said its estimates project Photoelectron will reach profitability in the second half of 1998. It has an 18- to 24-month target price of $17 for the stock.

-- Dain Bosworth said, however, that there are risks involved in investing in Photoelectron, including costs associated with commercializing the PRS and the lack of assurance the FDA will move quickly to approve the system.
-- Shares of Photoelectron traded up 1/4 at 8-1/4.
